intro: Day 1: Zion Canyon Visitor Center; Human History Museum. Day 2: Taylor Creek Trail. Day 3: Zion Human History Museum Patio. Day 4: Zion Nature Center; Human History Museum.

days.label: Zion Canyon orientation and the Towers of the Virgin

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Start with the outdoor exhibits and ask a ranger which canyon outings are accessible on your visit dates.
stops.why: It gives you a useful first look before committing the rest of your time.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Explore the indoor exhibits and, if showing, the 22-minute orientation film; step outside for views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain.
stops.why: The exhibits and the canyon scenery make this a satisfying, unhurried first day.

stops.name: Taylor Creek Trail
stops.note: Hike the Middle Fork of Taylor Creek past two homestead cabins toward Double Arch Alcove. Check trail conditions before setting out; wilderness groups are limited to 12 people.
stops.why: This Kolob Canyons hike offers a substantial, distinct outing through a creek canyon with historic cabins and a sandstone alcove.

stops.name: Zion Human History Museum Patio
stops.note: Step onto the museum patio for a short pause and take in the views of the Towers of the Virgin.
stops.why: It offers a relaxed, open-air look at Zion’s canyon scenery without adding a long hike to the day.

days.label: Zion Nature Center and canyon exhibits

stops.name: Zion Nature Center
stops.note: If your dates fall during its summer season and it is operating, explore the interactive exhibits on Zion's habitats and wildlife. Otherwise, use this time at the Human History Museum instead.
stops.why: This offers a different perspective on the canyon, especially if you'd like an easygoing final day.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Catch any exhibits or the orientation film you missed earlier, with another chance to enjoy the outside views.
stops.why: It provides a concrete option if the seasonal Nature Center isn't available.
